source_windows.description: Two white tones plus one black tone played harmonically; examples allow different hand allocations.
Reach out blindly for consonant or dissonant combinations; recap of both mixed-triple drills.

source_instructions: Play 2 white tones and 1 black tones together.
Use any keyboard location; reach out blindly rather than choosing only familiar consonances.
info.presentation: All three tones harmonically; hand arrangement is not fixed.

evidence.quote: different. We have white doubles at the same time as a black single. That means I'm playing
right now two white tones and one black tone. I'm playing E, A with my left hand and my
right hand is playing E flat. But you can do this anywhere on the keyboard. Anything
Anything you want.
Now I've got Eb, B in my left hand, and a D in my right hand.
So you're going to have two white tones and one black tone.
You can play them in any order you want, harmonically.
The second drill is just the reverse.
Two black tones and one white tone.
So play your dissonant chords and your harmonious chords, but actually you won't really be choosing.
You'll just be reaching out blindly and playing whatever you want.
So first we do two whites with one black, then we do two blacks with one white, all harmonically.
That's your assignment.
